description: We are Team MoSARltz from HCMC, Vietnam, specializing in Earth Sciences, SAR Remote Sensing, GIS, and Web Development. Passionate about urban climate and health, we built THE DENGUE WALTZ (mosarltz-nasa.netlify.app) using Sentinel-1/NISAR radar and HCDC data to forecast dengue outbreaks across 168 wards. Join us to turn NASA data into real-world impact! Seeking skills in: Epidemiology, Python/GEE automation, UI/UX design, and English pitching.
summary:
THE DENGUE WALTZ, developed by Team MoSARltz, is an interactive Web-GIS early warning platform (mosarltz-nasa.netlify.app) that forecasts dengue fever outbreaks across Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC). During tropical monsoons, persistent cloud cover blinds optical satellites, preventing authorities from detecting stagnant surface water that fuels Aedes mosquito breeding. Our solution overcomes this challenge by utilizing cloud-penetrating, all-weather Synthetic Aperture Radar (Sentinel-1 and NASA-ISRO NISAR) to identify flood pockets via low radar backscatter signals (around -18.6 dB).

By fusing SAR water masks with 30m Copernicus DEM topographic wetness (TWI), CHIRPS rainfall, Landsat 9 land surface temperature, and verified HCDC epidemiological data through a 7-step Negative Binomial Regression model (achieving an AUROC accuracy of 0.89), the platform predicts outbreak risks 2 to 4 weeks in advance across 168 restructured wards and flooded corridors like Tran Xuan Soan Street. In a megacity facing over 44,500 dengue cases, this proactive system empowers targeted vector control, citizen reporting, and emergency hospital routing before outbreaks peak.
details:
Project Overview: How It WorksTHE DENGUE WALTZ, developed by Team MoSARltz, is an interactive web-based geospatial decision-support platform designed to forecast dengue fever outbreaks across Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC). During the tropical monsoon season, persistent cloud cover blinds optical satellites, preventing health authorities from tracking surface water accumulation that fuels Aedes mosquito breeding. Our platform overcomes this barrier by leveraging all-weather, day-and-night Synthetic Aperture Radar (Sentinel-1 C-band and NASA-ISRO NISAR L/S-band). Flat standing water acts as a specular reflector, bouncing microwave pulses away from the sensor and registering low backscatter anomalies .

We fuse these radar water masks with 30m Copernicus DEM Topographic Wetness Index (TWI), CHIRPS/GPM precipitation, Landsat 9 Land Surface Temperature (LST), and historical epidemiological surveillance from the HCMC Center for Disease Control (HCDC, 2022–2026). Through a 7-step spatial pipeline—Zonal Statistics, Spearman rank correlation , Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) filtering, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and Negative Binomial Regression with a population offset—the platform computes Incidence Rate Ratios (IRR) and Moran’s I spatial autocorrelation to forecast outbreak clusters 2 to 4 weeks in advance.

Core Benefits & Expected Impact The platform shifts urban vector control from reactive post-outbreak spraying to proactive, data-driven early intervention:

  • For Health Authorities: Provides a 2-to-4-week ecological lead time to target larviciding and drainage maintenance across 168 newly restructured wards/communes (such as high-burden hotspots like Di An Ward with 861 cases) and specific inundated corridors like Tran Xuan Soan Street .
  • For Citizens & Schools: Delivers a 4-tier color-coded alert matrix, an interactive before/after SAR flood slider, and real-time Haversine emergency routing to tertiary hospitals.
  • Expected Impact: Directly supports a city experiencing over 44,500 cumulative cases by optimizing public health resource allocation, reducing hospital overload, and empowering residents to eliminate standing water before adult mosquitoes emerge.

Tools, Languages, Software & Hardware

  • Geospatial & Remote Sensing: QGIS, MapInfo Pro, Google Earth Engine, NASA Earthdata, and Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF DAAC) for processing SAR backscatter and DEM rasters.
  • Web Architecture & Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, modern JavaScript (ES6+), Leaflet.js for interactive multi-layer Web-GIS mapping, and Chart.js for multi-year time-series and ecological lag simulation.
  • Statistical Modeling & Deployment: Python for regression calibration and spatial statistics; GitHub and Netlify (mosarltz-nasa.netlify.app) for continuous cloud deployment; developed and tested on an Intel Core i5 / NVIDIA RTX workstation.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered Our primary innovation lies in bridging macro-scale orbital radar with hyper-local urban epidemiology. First, we built a spatial crosswalk that seamlessly translates 3-year historical district data into HCMC’s newly merged 168-ward administrative framework and pinpoints street-level tidal flood pockets. Second, we rigorously addressed scientific limitations: because ~10m C-band SAR cannot resolve micro-containers (flowerpots, tires) inside homes and suffers from urban radar shadow/double-bounce near high-rises, we integrated topographic wetness (TWI) alongside a Citizen Science Crowd-Reporting module for ground-truthing. Finally, we prioritized WCAG accessibility with clear text badges alongside color codes so every stakeholder can act swiftly.
